null_control_statement.statement: The accepted run has a null-implementation control on this build, docs/conformance/server-2026-07-28-null-control.json (a server answering -32601 to every method). Rows whose check it also passes carry null_passability, citing that scenario's entry there. A SUCCESS on such a row is not evidence of SDK behaviour.
null_control_statement.rule: A row's check is passed by the null server iff the null run names no failure or warning for it, the run emitted it, and the census's counts place it among the SUCCESS. Emitted: the locator's checks for the scenario, less any the emission reading says were not emitted, must number the run's total. Placed: the emitted checks, less the named failures and warnings, less any the reading assigns SKIPPED or INFO, must number exactly the SUCCESS count, and then each of them passed. Where total equals the locator's count and nothing is SKIPPED or INFO, the counts place every check with no reading. Otherwise a pinned reading, citing the harness bytes that emit or gate the check, supplies the rest; no reading, no claim.
null_control_statement.supersedes: For the combined bucket-2a view, this rule supersedes D2a-i's (PM ratification, MES-130 comment 29491, Q5). D2a-i's record is not edited. Gate 5 recomputes both slices by this rule and requires D2a-i's 16 unchanged.
null_control_statement.why_amended: D2a-i's rule, claiming the generic validator and every check of a scenario that failed nothing, goes wrong both ways on this slice. It over-claims server-sse-multiple-streams (failed nothing, yet reported an INFO) and under-claims dns-rebinding-protection and sep-2164-resource-not-found (each failed something, yet a non-validator check was among the SUCCESS). And it cannot place caching's SUCCESS (one SKIPPED) or tools-list's (a check not emitted). (MES-130 plan 29488, section 3.)

findings_for_pm: F1 (null rule): D2a-i's null_passability rule does not carry to this slice. It is amended to a counting rule with pinned emission readings for the combined view, and D2a-i's 16 are reproduced unchanged (29491, Q5). The sse pair, planned as null_indeterminate, is placed by the harness's status vocabulary instead; that deviation from 29491's wording is stated in null_control_statement.sse_pair.

F2 (ordering, MES-62 against the PO's Q2): HttpServerHeaderMismatch400 sends server/discover carrying an unsupported _meta version. MES-62's cross-check must therefore run on discover, and ahead of any version gate a YES to Q2 would add; otherwise the check earns -32022, not -32020. It is recorded on the row as a note and is not a landing condition.

F3 (possible SDK gap, no owner): ToolContext.log/4 does not consult the request's logLevel, so the MUST NOT falls on every handler. The adapter gates it by hand. It is routed for a decision, not given an owner here.
F4 (possible SDK gap, no owner): nothing in lib/ validates a tool name against SEP-986's format, and the SDK passes the handler's names through. It is routed for a decision.

F5 (latent defect): MCP.Protocol.Error.resource_not_found/1 sets data to the bare URI string, not a map carrying uri, so a handler using it once MES-43 comment 29490's slot lands would still earn the DataUri WARNING. It is unreachable from a handler today.
F6 (published artefact): report-2026-07-28.md's R4 row still reads UNOWNED. MES-62 is its owner now. The report was not edited.
